ChangeLog.description:
One change: when, by whom, what kind, and the fields that changed.

``diff`` is ``{field: [old, new]}`` minus the fields ``Karni.field_roles``
hides from the requesting user (P3), so history never shows a value the
row itself would not.

CheckoutInputRequest.description:
Input of ``POST /api/payments/checkout/``.

The amount is transport, not authority: the server-side
``KARNI_PAYMENTS_CHECKOUT_VALIDATOR`` decides whether it is acceptable
(amendment G2 — never trust client amounts).

CheckoutOutput.description: Output of the checkout action: redirect the customer to ``url``.

EmailChange.description:
Input for ``email/change/``: the new address plus the current password.

Uniqueness of ``new_email`` is validated (and re-validated at confirm
time) by :mod:`karni.accounts.services`, which raises the DRF 400
directly — the accepted enumeration surface of the flow (amendment A9).

EmailChangeRequest.description:

LoginRequest.description:
Credential check shared by both auth modes (amendment A3).

Inherits SimpleJWT's ``TokenObtainSerializer``: the fields are the user
model's ``USERNAME_FIELD`` (``email``) plus ``password``, credentials run
through ``django.contrib.auth.authenticate`` and a failure — wrong
password, unknown address or inactive account, indistinguishably — raises
``AuthenticationFailed`` (HTTP 401). ``validate`` issues no tokens; it
leaves the authenticated user on ``self.user`` and
:class:`karni.accounts.api.views.LoginView` decides per request whether to
mint a JWT pair or open a Django session.

LogoutRequest.description:
Input for ``logout/``: the refresh token to blacklist (JWT mode only).

The field is optional at this level because session mode posts an empty
body; the view enforces presence when ``KARNI_AUTH_MODE`` is ``"jwt"``.

Me.description:
The authenticated user's profile — the payload of ``me/`` and login.

Only the safe fields ``first_name`` / ``last_name`` are writable (the
``me/`` PATCH surface); ``email`` changes exclusively through the
email-change flow and everything else is audit data. ``roles`` (amendment
A15) lists the user's Django group names via
:func:`karni.accounts.permissions.user_roles` — the ``@karni/ui``
``usePermission`` hook consumes it.

Override / escape hatch: subclass and redeclare ``Meta.fields`` to expose
extra fields of a swapped user model, then point a subclassed view (or
``KARNI_ACCOUNTS_AUTO_LOGIN`` consumers) at your serializer.

roles.description: The user's role (Django group) names, read-only (amendment A15).

MeTerms.description:
Experimental. The ``terms`` of ``me/`` while ``KARNI_TERMS`` is set.

``required`` and ``accepted`` together say whether the API will refuse the
user (``E245``) until they accept ``version``, which is at ``url``.

TermsAcceptRequest.description:
Experimental. Request body of ``terms/accept/``: the version shown, and the client.

``version`` is the version the user read and accepted. ``client`` is an
optional JSON object the app sends about itself (a mobile app's device,
platform and app version, for example), stored with the acceptance. It
may be at most ``CLIENT_MAX_BYTES`` bytes of JSON.

TermsStatus.description:
Experimental. The answer of ``terms/`` and ``terms/accept/``.

``accepted_at`` is when the user accepted ``version``, ``null`` when they
have not. While ``required`` is true and ``accepted`` false, the API
refuses the user with ``E245``.

get.description:
``GET csrf/`` — CSRF cookie bootstrap for SPAs (amendment A4).

Returns 204 with the CSRF cookie set; a session-mode SPA calls this once
before its first credentialed POST and sends the cookie's value back in
the ``X-CSRFToken`` header. Harmless (and unnecessary) in JWT mode.

post.description:
``POST email/change/`` ``{new_email, current_password}`` — start the flow.

Auth plus the current password; the confirmation link is emailed to the
*new* address (clicking it proves ownership). A taken address is a 400
here and re-checked at confirm time (services layer, amendments A7/A9).

``POST email/change/confirm/`` ``{token}`` — finish the email change.

Anonymous on purpose: the emailed link lands on a frontend page without a
session. A uniqueness race between request and confirm surfaces as a 400
(``TokenError("invalid")``), never a 500 (amendment A7).
``POST email/verify/`` ``{token}`` — confirm ownership of the address.

``POST email/verify/resend/`` — email a fresh verification link.

Auth required, so it may answer honestly (amendment A9): an
already-verified account gets a 200 saying so instead of pointless mail.
Reissuing invalidates the previously emailed link (single active token
per purpose).

``POST login/`` — authenticate with email and password (both modes).

JWT mode → ``{"access", "refresh", "user"}``; session mode → Django
session plus ``{"user"}``. When the account has confirmed 2FA the
response is the gate payload (``requires_2fa`` + ``ephemeral_token``) and
*no* credentials — see :func:`_twofa_gate_payload`. ``ensure_csrf_cookie``
guarantees SPAs a CSRF cookie from the very first auth call (amendment
A4); the per-account throttle rides alongside the per-IP one (A5).

``POST logout/`` — end the current credential.

JWT mode blacklists the posted refresh token (the short-lived access
token expires on its own — by design, amendment A1's documented window);
session mode flushes the Django session. 204 on success.

get.description:
``GET``/``PATCH me/`` — the authenticated user's profile.

PATCH accepts only the safe fields (``first_name`` / ``last_name``);
everything else in :class:`MeSerializer` is read-only, and read-only
fields in a payload are ignored, not errors. PUT is deliberately absent —
the profile is never wholly replaced through this endpoint.

patch.description:
``GET``/``PATCH me/`` — the authenticated user's profile.

PATCH accepts only the safe fields (``first_name`` / ``last_name``);
everything else in :class:`MeSerializer` is read-only, and read-only
fields in a payload are ignored, not errors. PUT is deliberately absent —
the profile is never wholly replaced through this endpoint.

post.description:
Experimental. ``POST otp/send/`` ``{email}``: email a sign-in code, enumeration-silent.

Always the same 200 and the same body (:func:`karni.accounts.otp.send_answer`:
``{"detail", "length", "expires_in"}``), whether the address has an
account, is inactive, or may not sign up. :func:`karni.accounts.otp.send_code`
does the same work on every path and sends the email after the
transaction commits. A malformed address is a plain 400. While
``KARNI_EMAIL_OTP`` is off the route is not mounted, and a URLconf built
earlier answers 404 ``E236``.

Throttled per IP (``auth.otp_send``) and per address
(``auth.otp_send_email``). Override / escape hatch: subclass and declare
``path("api/auth/otp/send/", ...)`` before the include, or change
``throttle_classes`` / ``throttle_scope``.

Experimental. ``POST otp/verify/`` ``{email, code}``: sign in with the emailed code.

The answer is the one ``login/`` gives: ``{"access", "refresh", "user"}``
in JWT mode, a session plus ``{"user"}`` in session mode, or the 2FA gate
payload (:func:`_twofa_gate_payload`). When the code verified an address
that was never verified, it also removed the account's password, and the
answer adds ``"password_removed": true`` so the app can say so. A refused code is a 401 ``E235``
whatever went wrong (wrong, expired, used, locked, or an address nobody
sent a code to), an inactive account a 401 ``E226`` after a right code,
and a new account under the ``approval`` policy a 202 ``E224`` with no
credentials. Refusals are returned, not raised, so a guess spent on a
wrong code stays spent even with ``ATOMIC_REQUESTS``.

Throttled per IP (``auth.otp_verify``), on top of the attempt cap of each
code. Override / escape hatch: subclass and declare
``path("api/auth/otp/verify/", ...)`` before the include.

``POST password/change/`` — rotate the password (auth required).

Requires the current password. On success every outstanding refresh token
is blacklisted (amendment A1 — stolen refresh tokens die with the old
credential; access tokens live out their short lifetime by design), and in
session mode ``update_session_auth_hash`` keeps the changer's own session
alive while every other session's auth hash goes stale.

``POST password/reset/`` — request a reset link, enumeration-silent.

Always 200 with the same body whether or not the address has an account
(amendment A9): the only reset endpoint that must never reveal existence.

``POST password/reset/confirm/`` — set a new password via the link.

Token consumption, password validation and the amendment-A1 refresh-token
blacklisting all happen atomically in
:func:`karni.accounts.services.confirm_password_reset`; a rejected
password rolls back and leaves the token usable (amendment A7).

get.description: ``GET permissions/effective/[<user id>/]`` — what a user may do, and why.
``GET permissions/effective/[<user id>/]`` — what a user may do, and why.
``GET``/``POST permissions/matrix/`` — the matrix, and changes to it.

post.description: ``GET``/``POST permissions/matrix/`` — the matrix, and changes to it.

``POST refresh/`` — rotate a refresh token (JWT mode only).

Session mode answers 405 from the view (amendment A3 — the URL exists in
both modes): the session cookie is the credential there and renews
itself. JWT mode delegates to SimpleJWT's ``TokenRefreshView``; with
Karni's conf defaults refresh tokens rotate and the old one is
blacklisted (``ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS`` / ``BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION``).

``POST register/`` — create an account, 201 with the profile payload.

The response body is the :class:`MeSerializer` payload of the new user.
With ``KARNI_ACCOUNTS_AUTO_LOGIN = True`` (default ``False``) the response
additionally carries ``access``/``refresh`` in JWT mode, or opens a
session in session mode. The verification email goes out on transaction
commit (amendment A7) through the configured accounts email backend.

get.description:
Experimental. ``GET terms/``: the current terms, and whether the user accepted them.

``{"version", "url", "required", "accepted", "accepted_at"}``
(:func:`karni.accounts.terms.status`). 401 without a signed-in user. The
route exists while ``KARNI_TERMS`` is set, and a URLconf built earlier
answers 404 ``E249`` once it is unset. The terms gate never refuses it.

Override / escape hatch: subclass and declare ``path("api/auth/terms/",
...)`` before the include.

post.description:
Experimental. ``POST terms/accept/`` ``{version, client?}``: accept the current terms.

Records the acceptance (:func:`karni.accounts.terms.accept`) with the
client's IP (read like the throttles read it, honouring ``NUM_PROXIES``),
its ``User-Agent`` and the optional ``client`` object, and answers 201
with the ``terms/`` body. The same version again answers 200 and changes
nothing. Another version is a 400 ``E246`` carrying the current
``version`` and ``url``, and nothing is recorded. 401 without a signed-in
user, 404 ``E249`` from a URLconf built while ``KARNI_TERMS`` was set.

Override / escape hatch: subclass and declare
``path("api/auth/terms/accept/", ...)`` before the include, or call
:func:`karni.accounts.terms.accept` from a view of your own.

get.description: ``GET /<resource>/import/<job>/``: the job's state and progress.

post.description: ``POST /<resource>/import/<job>/commit/``: write it, after a preview, atomically.

``POST /<resource>/import/<job>/preview/``: the dry run, with ``{"mapping": …}``.

``"match_ids": true`` matches existing rows by the file's id column, and
``"keep_ids": true`` creates rows with the file's ids (both off by default).

Every row is validated and written inside a transaction that is
rolled back, so the counts and the per-row errors are exactly what
the commit will do. Large files run in Celery: poll the job.

get.description:
``GET /<resource>/<id>/history/``: the row's field-level changes, newest first.

Answers only for models that opt in with ``class Karni: audit = True``
(404 otherwise, saying so). The row is looked up through the read
scope, so an unreadable row is a 404 like everywhere else, and each
entry's diff omits the fields ``Karni.field_roles`` hides from the
requester.

get.description:
Read-only refunds, gated on the ``payments-admin`` role.

``HasRole`` is both the request gate (non-admins get 403) and the row
policy (non-admins would see no rows even if the gate were swapped).

Override / escape hatch: to let customers list their own refunds,
subclass with ``access = Access(read=Owned("payment__user") |
HasRole("payments-admin"), write=HasRole("payments-admin"))``.
